Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

1: # Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
6: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
7: printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
8: \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
9: Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).
10: 
11: > 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
12: > prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.
13: 
14: ## Definitions and complete target
15: 
16: Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
17: \(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
18: Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
19: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
20: of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy
21: 
22: \[
23: [h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
24: \]
25: 
26: Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
27: \(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
28: the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
29: \(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
30: An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
31: subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
32: \(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.
33: 
34: Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
35: \(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
36: acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
37: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
38: Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
39: invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
40: Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
41: algebraically closed.
42: 
43: ## Fixed natural-language proof
44: 
45: ### 1. Divided-power coordinates in characteristic zero
46: 
47: Put \(n=\lambda+1\) and \(e_i=y^iv/i!\) for \(0\leq i\leq\lambda\).
48: The commutator identities give, by induction,
49: 
50: \[
51: hy^iv=(\lambda-2i)y^iv,\qquad
52: xy^iv=i(\lambda-i+1)y^{i-1}v\quad(i\geq1).
53: \]
54: 
55: For \(i\leq\lambda\), applying \(x^i\) to \(y^iv\) gives
56: \(i!\lambda(\lambda-1)\cdots(\lambda-i+1)v\ne0\) over \(\mathbb C\).
57: At \(i=0\) the empty product is one. Thus every \(e_i\ne0\).
58: Their \(h\)-eigenvalues \(\lambda-2i\) are distinct over \(\mathbb C\),
59: so they are linearly independent: applying
60: \(\prod_{k\ne j}(h-(\lambda-2k)\mathrm{Id})\) to a relation isolates
61: its \(j\)-th coefficient with a nonzero multiplier.
62: There are \(n\) vectors, the dimension of \(V(\lambda)\), hence they
63: form a basis. Also \(y^{\lambda+1}v=0\), since otherwise it would be
64: an eigenvector of eigenvalue \(-\lambda-2\), absent from this basis.
65: All higher lowering powers vanish as well.
66: 
67: The operator matrices are therefore
68: 
69: \[
70: xe_0=0,\quad xe_i=(\lambda-i+1)e_{i-1}\ (i\geq1),\qquad
71: ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1}\ (i<\lambda),\quad ye_\lambda=0,
72: \quad he_i=(\lambda-2i)e_i.
73: \]
74: 
75: Iteration gives the integral divided-power matrices
76: 
77: \[
78: X_re_i=\binom{\lambda-i+r}{r}e_{i-r}\quad(0\leq r\leq i),
79: \qquad
80: Y_re_i=\binom{i+r}{r}e_{i+r}\quad(i+r\leq\lambda).       \tag{1}
81: \]
82: 
83: The respective expressions are zero when \(r>i\) or
84: \(i+r>\lambda\), by termination of the strings just proved.
85: 
86: ### 2. Matrix units preserve the localized arbitrary lattice
87: 
88: Let \(R=\mathbb Z_{(p)}=\{a/b\in\mathbb Q:p\nmid b\}\), and regard
89: \(M_R=R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}M\) as a submodule of \(V(\lambda)\).
90: The embedding is injective because an integer basis of \(M\) is
91: complex-linearly independent. The module \(M_R\) is free of rank \(n\)
92: over \(R\) and is preserved by all \(X_r,Y_r\), by admissibility.
93: 
94: Define \(E_{ij}\) to send \(e_j\) to \(e_i\) and all other basis
95: vectors to zero. Formula (1) gives
96: 
97: \[
98: P:=Y_\lambda X_\lambda=E_{\lambda\lambda},\qquad
99: X_{\lambda-i}P=E_{i\lambda},\qquad
100: P Y_{\lambda-j}=\binom\lambda j E_{\lambda j}.
101: \]
102: 
103: For the last identity, an input index below \(j\) is sent below
104: \(e_\lambda\) and killed by \(P\); an index above \(j\) is sent past
105: the end of the lowering string. On \(e_j\) the coefficient is precisely
106: \(\binom\lambda j\). Since \(\lambda<p\), none of
107: \(\lambda!\), \(j!\), \((\lambda-j)!\) is divisible by \(p\), so
108: \(\binom\lambda j\) is a unit in \(R\). Consequently
109: 
110: \[
111: E_{ij}=\left(\binom\lambda j\right)^{-1}
112:        X_{\lambda-i}P Y_{\lambda-j}.                 \tag{2}
113: \]
114: 
115: Every matrix unit preserves \(M_R\). No assertion about distinct
116: weights modulo \(p\) has been used.
117: 
118: ### 3. Recover a standard basis for the arbitrary lattice
119: 
120: Define \(J_i=\{c\in\mathbb C:c e_i\in M_R\}\).
121: The coordinate projection \(E_{ii}\) maps \(M_R\) onto \(J_i e_i\).
122: Applying \(E_{ij}\) to \(c e_j\) shows \(J_j\subseteq J_i\);
123: reversing the indices gives equality. Let \(J\) be their common module.
124: It is finitely generated, being a projection of a finite free module,
125: and nonzero because \(M_R\) spans \(V(\lambda)\) over \(\mathbb C\).
126: The coordinate projections and independence of the \(e_i\) give
127: 
128: \[
129: M_R=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{\lambda}J e_i.                  \tag{3}
130: \]
131: 
132: One must still prove that \(J\) has rank one; containment in
133: \(\mathbb C\) alone does not imply that. Let
134: \(r=\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J)\), which is finite.
135: Tensoring (3) with the fraction field \(\mathbb Q\) and using the
136: rank \(n\) of \(M_R\) gives \(n=nr\), so \(r=1\), since \(n>0\).
137: The multiplication map \(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J\to\mathbb C\) is
138: injective: this tensor product is the localization of the torsion-free
139: module \(J\subset\mathbb C\), and a fraction mapping to zero has
140: zero numerator. Thus \(J\) spans a one-dimensional rational line.
141: 
142: Choose \(0\ne a\in J\) and write a finite set of nonzero generators
143: as \(q_1a,\ldots,q_ka\) with \(q_j\in\mathbb Q^\times\).
144: Each \(q_j=p^{\nu_j}u_j\) for \(\nu_j\in\mathbb Z\) and a unit
145: \(u_j\) of \(R\). Let \(\nu=\min_j\nu_j\). All generators belong
146: to \(p^\nu R a\), and a generator with minimal exponent generates
147: that whole module. Therefore \(J=Rb\) for a nonzero \(b\in J\).
148: By (3), \(b e_0,\ldots,b e_\lambda\) is an \(R\)-basis of \(M_R\).
149: 
150: ### 4. Reduce and extend scalars
151: 
152: All denominators in \(R\) are invertible in \(K\), so the integer map
153: extends to \(R\to K\). The natural tensor maps give
154: 
155: \[
156: M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\cong M_R\otimes_R K
157: \cong(M_R/pM_R)\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}K.
158: \]
159: 
160: For example the first map sends \(m\otimes c\) to
161: \((1\otimes m)\otimes c\); its inverse sends
162: \((r\otimes m)\otimes c\) to \(m\otimes\bar r c\).
163: The reduced images \(b_0,\ldots,b_\lambda\) of \(b e_i\) form a
164: \(K\)-basis, with exactly the matrices of step 1 reduced into \(K\).
165: The matrix-unit identities (2) persist on this basis.
166: 
167: For \(0\leq r\leq\lambda<p\), \(r!\ne0\) in \(K\), and the induced
168: \(X_r,Y_r\) equal \((r!)^{-1}x^r,(r!)^{-1}y^r\). Hence any
169: \(K\)-subspace invariant under \(x,y\) is invariant under every matrix
170: unit in (2).
171: 
172: ### 5. Conclude irreducibility
173: 
174: Let \(W\) be invariant. If it is nonzero, choose
175: \(0\ne w=\sum_i c_i b_i\in W\), and an index \(j\) with \(c_j\ne0\).
176: For every \(i\), \(E_{ij}w=c_jb_i\in W\). Division by \(c_j\)
177: gives \(b_i\in W\), so all basis vectors lie in \(W\) and
178: \(W=V(K)\). Since \(\dim_K V(K)=\lambda+1>0\), it is nonzero and
179: irreducible. If \(\lambda=0\), all relevant factorials and binomial
180: coefficients are one and the argument applies unchanged. For \(p=2\),
181: the allowed \(\lambda\) are zero and one; the proof still works
182: without requiring distinct reduced \(h\)-eigenvalues.
183:

20: `basis-registry.json`, retained source evidence and `proof-context.json`.
21: Its global lane checks original-target fidelity, replacement dependencies and
22: structure; ordinary local R lanes check all new arguments. There is no preceding
23: full mathematical audit of 2basis. NL0 faithfully presents the active basis route,
24: without requiring the original proof route to remain unchanged. Review reuse
25: includes active context; source warnings retain their original qualification.
26: 
27: ## Submission schema
28: 
29: Submit an object with exactly:
30: 
31: ```text
32: version: "yui-basis-1"
33: full_target: exact target-selection.json full_target
34: proof: complete basis-reduced natural-language proof
35: lean_header: "import Mathlib\n" followed by needed object definitions
36: dependencies: [dependency, ...]
37: replacements: [{original_dependency, replacement:[B IDs], explanation}, ...]
38: ```
39: 
40: Each dependency has exactly:
41: 
42: ```text
43: id: B001 (three or more digits)
44: category: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4
45: statement: complete mathematical statement
46: origin: {kind, reference, revision, evidence:[evidence reference, ...]}
47: compatibility: native | adapted | internal | unresolved
48: uses: [other B IDs]
49: port: E001 | M001 | null
50: lean: {type: closed Lean proposition, proof: tactic body after "by"} | null
51: justification: actual source/reduction/compatibility account
52: ```
53: 
54: Origin kinds are `mathlib`, `lean-library`, `derivation`, `textbook`, respectively.
55: Reference identifies the actual declaration/public source/theorem or derivation;
56: revision identifies its version/edition. Category and compatibility are distinct:
57: a Mathlib result from another version is still class 1, possibly `adapted`.
58: 
59: - Class 1/native: direct Mathlib (`port:null`) or optional M port.
60: - Class 1/adapted and class 2: provisional E port with actual checked proof in
61:   the pinned target environment. Prepare needed adapters and retained source
62:   attribution now; no whole-library migration prerequisite.
63: - Class 3: `internal`, `port:null`, `lean:null`, nonempty `uses`. Give a concrete
64:   derivation in the proof, recursively from 1/2 via other 3, with no unresolved
65:   4. Existing NL0/T workers prove it internally; it cannot become an E premise.
66: - Class 4: `unresolved`, E port, `lean:{type,proof:null}`. Retain a verified
67:   complete textbook theorem and evidence. Missing sources, contradictions,
68:   unspecified statements and internal proof gaps are not 4.
69: 
70: `uses` records genuine dependencies; unknown IDs and cycles are rejected.
71: Prepared 1/2 proofs may refer to other prepared 1/2 proofs as `YuiBasis.Bddd`.
72: Their closed types bind their own parameters/typeclasses, without project H/E.
73: Use inline local Lean constructions for private helpers. All used 1/2 proofs
74: must compile and pass dependency/axiom inspection in 2basis. The header contains
75: object definitions, not axioms, theorem declarations or executable metaprogramming.
76: 
77: Evidence is `{input:"declared-document-ID"}` or an actual retained own-stage
78: `{path,sha256}`. Class 4 requires evidence. References bind actual bytes;
79: the basis reviewer checks source completeness and classification before release. The shared Audit A also reviews the actual later uses.
80: 
81: Use `base_candidate:N` with JSON-pointer patches into the basis object, or
82: `accept_candidate:N`. `base_input:"prior-basis.json"` continues user-requested
83: reduction. Every revised artifact receives the same real native checks.
84: Compiler/resource nonpass is feedback, not mathematical impossibility.
85: 
86: For long reductions, `save_basis_draft` saves partial work without running Lean;
87: `read_basis_draft` reads only that author's actual saved candidates, with bounded
88: JSON-pointer pagination. A context-reset checkpoint names the newest draft and
89: last machine-checked candidate separately. Saving does not make a proof complete.
90: 
91: ## Early statement and use review
92: 
93: Only a submitted, machine-checked basis enters the separate basis reviewer role.
94: It compares classes 1, 2 and 4 together against the original sources, the
95: rewritten use and the propositions printed by Lean. For class 4 it reads the
96: value of the proposition definition. The comparison covers quantifier order,
97: uniform constants, domains, assumptions, direction, definitions and adapters.
98: Class 3 derivations go to the ordinary NL0 and Lean workers.
99: 
100: The reviewer submits a located PASS, FAIL or UNVERIFIED for every assigned item.
101: A normal-policy nonpass goes back to the same basis author with the prior
102: artifact and findings. First-pass policy retains the first nonpass. Saving or
103: checking drafts costs no reviewer call. Each submitted revision uses at most
104: one review batch. An empty scope uses zero calls. Exact previous assessments
105: can be reused within the case when their sources, rules, shared route and
106: connected dependencies and uses still match. Unchanged rejected work retains
107: its findings and pauses. The execution ledger includes both roles.
108: 
109: The active context binds the selected basis, native check and semantic report.
110: Downstream readback verifies their inputs and the reviewer's complete submission.
111: Historical native-only contexts use their original runtime snapshots.
112: 
113: ## Remaining class 4 and errors
114: 
115: The existing retained controller records an exact `basis-decision` incident.
116: Only explicit user choices authorize these commands:
117: 
118: ```sh
119: python3 -B nl0/scripts/yui.py basis-decision RUN --incident ID --action stop
120: python3 -B nl0/scripts/yui.py basis-decision RUN --incident ID --action continue
121: python3 -B nl0/scripts/yui.py basis-decision RUN --incident ID --action accept-conditional
122: ```
123: 
124: Continue retains the author/prior artifact. Accept binds exact residual IDs and
125: artifact, without approving future additions. Stop records an unfinished
126: user-stopped outcome and releases owned roles. The batch reads its incident and
127: control after case exit and admits the next queued case. A case deadline also
128: applies while the operator choice is pending. Stale/changed/dead-owner decisions
129: are rejected. No silent conditional fallback.
130: 
131: Transport faults, cancellation, budgets and native limits use existing handling.
132: Unexpected faults retain evidence at PAUSED_ERROR, without authorizing cleanup
133: of real runs. Test cleanup is a separate test-only boundary.
134: 
135: ## Explicit revision of a downstream basis defect
136: 
137: If a global NL0 or interface role finds a conflict in a frozen B statement or
138: Lean type, use `report_basis_defect`. Identify the exact field and value, quote
139: the original source and the affected use, and explain the correction. A local
140: proof worker can send a connection problem through its existing diagnosis
141: route. The global reporting stage checks the citations against the documents it
142: was given. A valid report pauses the case as `BASIS_REVISION_REQUIRED`.
143: 
144: Inspect the finding before choosing a revision. To continue, cancel the paused
145: case, wait for the case and its worker processes to exit, then run
146: 
147: ```sh
148: python3 -B nl0/scripts/yui.py resume RUN --repair-basis --prepare-only
149: python3 -B nl0/scripts/yui.py execute NEW_RUN
150: ```
151: 
152: The new job starts from the previous basis and the located objection under the
153: original target, profiles, policy, worker limit and deadline. The prior run keeps
154: its evidence and costs. The revised basis must pass the native and correspondence
155: checks, including a response to the objection for a retained formal item. New
156: NL0, Audit A, interface, proof and final checks follow. If the old round had
157: completed local Lean bodies, an identical local program and use context may
158: supply a candidate after the new interface freeze. The proof queue checks it
159: with the current kernel before skipping a worker. Audit A's whole-context
160: binding invalidates the previous acceptance. Any new residual choice requires
161: its own operator decision.
162: 
163: ## Shared translation and final closure
164: 
165: The interface author receives prepared basis header/E types. Preserve that
166: header prefix and exact E types; independently review the NL/Lean correspondence
167: before freezing. Original H and whole target retain ordinary semantic review.
168: All shared proof, repair, assembly and worker machinery is reused.
169: 
170: After machine Audit B, b2lean applies prepared 1/2 proofs to `AuditBExport.P` and
171: generates `YuiClosed.P`, with only H and explicitly approved 4. Compile the final
172: standalone source and inspect its actual full signature and transitive trust.
173: An old conditional receipt cannot establish final closure. No final NL model.
174: Missing proofs, extra premises, signature/source/version drift, unexpected axioms
175: or incomplete inspection fail acceptance.
176: An exception with unconfirmed native shutdown retains a marked workspace and
177: diagnostic for owned cleanup; normal completed native checks release scratch.
178: 
179: `b2lean/Proof.lean`, `check.json` and `report.json` bind the final export.
180: Only closed output with unqualified upstream authority is `UNCONDITIONAL_LEAN`

183: `closure.kernel_closed:true` but no unconditional workflow acceptance. Both
184: qualified cases remain `WORKFLOW-CONDITIONAL`, with warnings and an unmet
185: unconditional goal. Interface drift cannot inherit exact frozen closure.

3: <!-- yui-nl0-acceptance:begin -->
4: ## Shared mathematical acceptance requirements
5: 
6: Contract version: `yui-nl0-audit-a-2`.
7: 
8: The author and independent auditor use this same mathematical standard. NL0
9: reviews a complete natural-language proof and necessary mathematical detail.
10: Specific Lean declarations, signatures, representations and proof tactics are
11: implementation work for nl02lean, not prerequisites for ordinary NL0 review.
12: The following grouped criteria replace V1's ten separate per-R report rows.
13: 
14: | ID | Review group | Author evidence group | Requirement |
15: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
16: | `target` | package | original_context_note | Preserve the complete original theorem, every original H, quantifier, domain, normalization, parameter range, constant dependency and supplied active proof route. In explicit 2basis mode, the original task remains target/H authority and the basis proof is the authorized active route; review both, including replacements and new derivations. A parameter or definition cannot hide a hypothesis or desired conclusion. |
17: | `definitions` | package | declaration_check | Define mathematical objects and notation sufficiently for their actual uses. Check types, dependencies, construction guards and legitimate local introductions. A definition grants no unproved property. |
18: | `sources` | package | original_context_note | Check complete E statements, primary-source identity, context and conditions under the source policy. Unavailable originals remain disclosed UNVERIFIED source assumptions. |

25: ### Scope and mathematical boundary
26: 
27: Global review owns target/H fidelity, definitions, source statements and graph
28: consistency. Each local reviewer owns the conditional implication at its R
29: node. Conditional packet replay has a different input boundary: these statements are conditional premises.
30: The local reviewer does not re-prove an input N or re-audit its source paper;
31: the graph and that producer's review establish those separate obligations.
32: Conversely, an input N exports only its full statement, not unexported facts
33: from the producer's body. The fifth local criterion, packet_replay, assesses
34: sufficiency under this exact boundary. The controller records execution
35: identity and exposure independently of the mathematical judgment.
36: 
37: Review correctness rather than the number of displayed lines. Ordinary valid
38: textbook compression is allowed. Material missing hypotheses, witnesses,
39: constructions, scope discharges or core arguments are not implementation gaps.
40: Return them for located author repair and fresh review. No theorem needs to be re-proved
41: when its legitimate mathematical source and actual application suffice.
42: 
43: The domain-neutral elementary-language-4 profile retains equality, supplied
44: definitions, finite arithmetic/order reasoning and finite sums. It is syntax
45: and elementary calculation policy, not a subject vocabulary or theorem list.
46: Objects from any field use problem parameters, D definitions or scoped locals.
47: Neither an author-written calculation list nor a familiar symbol adds a theorem.

49: ### Mathematical background: mathematical-background-v2-1
50: 
51: A reviewer may positively assess a routine, local mathematical fact without
52: first finding its Mathlib declaration. Record its precise mathematical
53: statement, actual argument location, available condition grounds and a short
54: mathematical justification in a background note. Use kind mathematical for an
55: ordinary background result and elementary for a useful elementary completion.
56: This is an actual mathematical judgment, not a future TODO or a claim of

61: Important external tools remain explicit E inputs; a missing project result

68: detailed-NL0 format-3 native-background receipt. At nl02lean, workers must discharge all necessary
69: facts by actual Lean proofs or checked library use; a note never becomes an
70: unproved H, axiom or extra external assumption. The exact implementation may
71: differ while preserving the mathematical meaning.

75: Independent reviewers assess the actual content; schema validation does not

Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

This proof retains exactly the original target and standing hypotheses. Fix any prime p, any field K of characteristic p, any integer λ with 0≤λ<p, the given complex irreducible highest-weight sl2-module V=V(λ) of dimension λ+1, its Chevalley operators x,y,h satisfying [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h, the given v≠0 with xv=0 and hv=λv, and ANY admissible lattice M of the problem. All divided powers X_r=x^r/r!, Y_r=y^r/r! for r≥0 preserve M by its U_Z-stability. Products of endomorphisms act rightmost first. Write l for the natural number equal to the nonnegative integer λ, and n=l+1. This is only a change of index domain, not a change of the parameter range. Integers in complex formulas are cast into C, and integers in reduced formulas are cast into K. The highest-weight module's irreducibility is retained as an original hypothesis; the calculation below needs only its stated dimension, commutators and highest-weight vector. No assumption of algebraic closure of K, and no restriction excluding p=2, is made.

The proof replaces the localization, fractional-ideal and localized-basis steps by integral multiples of matrix units followed directly by scalar extension. No new external theorem assumption is introduced. B001--B005 are the prepared native Mathlib facts. B101--B105 are internal lemmas proved here, not additional premises. Ordinary vector-space, tensor-product and finite-sum identities below are used with their defining algebraic properties; the registry is not a restriction on access to Mathlib.

B101: characteristic-zero string calculations and the divided-power basis.
For every i≥0, the commutator identities and induction give
h y^i v=(l-2i)y^i v,
x y^i v=i(l-i+1)y^{i-1}v for i≥1.
For completeness the h induction uses hy=yh-2y. For the x induction, x y^{i+1}v=(yx+h)y^i v, so the coefficient is i(l-i+1)+(l-2i)=(i+1)(l-i). The initial identities use xv=0 and hv=lv. These recurrences hold without assuming any termination of the y string.

For 0≤i≤l put e_i=(i!)^{-1}y^i v. Repeated use of the x recurrence gives
x^i y^i v=i! [l(l-1)...(l-i+1)] v.
The empty product for i=0 is one. Each factor in the nonempty descending product is a positive integer, hence nonzero in C, so e_i≠0 and x^i e_i=[l!/(l-i)!]v≠0. Also x^{i+1}e_i=0, since x^i e_i is a scalar multiple of v. To prove independence, suppose Σ_{i=0}^l c_i e_i=0 is a relation with a nonzero coefficient and choose its largest index m with c_m≠0. Applying x^m kills every term with index less than m; terms with index greater than m already have coefficient zero. It gives c_m [l!/(l-m)!]v=0, a contradiction. The family is therefore linearly independent, and B001 with dim_C V=n gives span equal to V; it is a basis.

Let u=y^{l+1}v. The same h recurrence gives hu=(-l-2)u. Expand u=Σ_i t_i e_i in the basis. Since he_i=(l-2i)e_i, comparison of coefficients gives 2(l+1-i)t_i=0 for every 0≤i≤l. This is a nonzero complex multiplier, so every t_i=0. Thus u=0, and all higher y powers of v vanish. The x recurrence and the definition of e_i now give
xe_0=0, xe_i=(l-i+1)e_{i-1} (1≤i≤l),
ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} (i<l), ye_l=0,
he_i=(l-2i)e_i.
Iterating the first and second formulas and dividing by r! in C yields
X_r e_i=choose(l-i+r,r)e_{i-r} if r≤i, and zero if r>i;
Y_r e_i=choose(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r≤l, and zero otherwise.
Indeed the first coefficient before division by r! is the product (l-i+1)...(l-i+r), and the second is (i+1)...(i+r); their factorial quotients are the displayed binomial coefficients. When the indices leave the string, a zero endpoint is encountered. This also proves the formulas for r=0, where both operators are the identity. This proves B101 from the elementary recurrences and B001.

B102: integral multiples of all matrix units.
Let E_ij be the complex-linear map taking e_j to e_i and all other e_k to zero, for 0≤i,j≤l. These are definitions relative to the basis just proved. Set
P=Y_l X_l, c_j=choose(l,j), a_j=j!(l-j)!, d=l!,
T_ij=X_{l-i} P Y_{l-j}, Q_ij=a_j T_ij.
All indices in these products are nonnegative and at most l. X_l kills e_k for k<l and sends e_l to e_0, and Y_l sends e_0 to e_l, so P=E_ll. Moreover X_{l-i} e_l=e_i. If k<j, Y_{l-j} e_k either lies strictly below e_l or is zero; if k>j, it is zero because the index is past l; on e_j it equals c_j e_l. Hence T_ij=c_j E_ij. The ordinary factorial identity
j!(l-j)! choose(l,j)=l!
for j≤l now gives the exact identity Q_ij=d E_ij in End_C(V).

Every factor X_r,Y_r preserves M, and a_j is an integer, so Q_ij restricts to a Z-linear endomorphism of M. On V the basis calculation gives E_ij E_kt=δ_jk E_it and Σ_i E_ii=Id. Thus, on M, the restricted operators satisfy
Q_ij Q_kt = d Q_it if j=k, and 0 if j≠k,
Σ_i Q_ii=d Id_M.
To justify restriction of identities, evaluate the equal complex maps on m∈M; the inclusion M⊆V is injective, so the values agree already in M. There is no division by d on M in this step. The same restriction argument gives r! X_r=x^r and r! Y_r=y^r on M for all natural r, directly from the definitions in C. Here x=X_1 and y=Y_1; h preserves M as well since h=xy-yx. These restrictions are the original lattice operators. This proves B102 using B101.

The given integer basis of M is also a complex basis of V. It therefore has exactly n elements: the finite-dimensional complex basis-cardinality theorem B005 gives this after indexing it by its finite cardinality. A basis of a finite-dimensional space is finite, so the indexing set can be replaced by Fin n. This is a reindexing of the given arbitrary lattice basis, not the choice of the minimal divided-power lattice. In particular M has a Z-basis indexed by Fin n.

B103: scalar extension, tensor-order compatibility, and normalized matrix units.
Use N=K⊗_Z M as the working representation of the original V(K)=M⊗_Z K. Here K is a Z-algebra through its integer map. The maps
τ:M⊗_Z K→K⊗_Z M, τ(m⊗c)=c⊗m,
σ:K⊗_Z M→M⊗_Z K, σ(c⊗m)=m⊗c
are defined by the balanced bilinear maps on pure tensors. For z∈Z, the balance check is c⊗(zm)=(zc)⊗m, and the reverse map has the same check. The K-action on the original tensor product is on its K factor. Both maps commute with that action, as may be checked on m⊗c and then finite sums. Their composites are the identity on pure tensors and hence on the whole tensor products. Thus τ is a K-linear isomorphism. For every integer endomorphism f of M it intertwines m⊗c↦f(m)⊗c with c⊗m↦c⊗f(m); again this is the same equality on each pure tensor. This establishes compatibility with the original action, rather than changing the reduction being studied.

By B002 an integer basis b_0,...,b_l of M gives the K-basis 1⊗b_0,...,1⊗b_l of N. By B005, dim_K N=n; this basis also makes N finite-dimensional. It is nonempty (n=l+1>0) and its vectors are nonzero, so N≠0.

Let F:End_Z(M)→End_K(N) be the Z-algebra homomorphism of B003 and put a bar over the scalar-extended lattice maps. B003 transports sums, compositions, powers, the identity and integer scalar multiples. B004, applied to r=l<p, says that d_K, the image of d=l! in K, is a unit and in particular nonzero. Define
A_ij=d_K^{-1} overline(Q_ij).
Transporting the integral identities of B102 gives
overline(Q_ij) overline(Q_kt)=δ_jk d_K overline(Q_it),
Σ_i overline(Q_ii)=d_K Id_N.
Scalar multiplication commutes with K-linear endomorphisms, so multiplication by d_K^{-2} in the first equality and d_K^{-1} in the second yields
A_ij A_kt=δ_jk A_it,  Σ_i A_ii=Id_N.
This proves B103 with B002--B005 and the integral identities as its stated premises; its proof applies to any integral module and operators satisfying those premises.

B104: invariance under the original generators implies invariance under these matrix units.
For every 0≤r≤l<p, B004 gives r! nonzero in K. Applying B003 to the restricted factorial identities of B102 gives
(r! in K) overline(X_r)=overline(x)^r,
(r! in K) overline(Y_r)=overline(y)^r.
Consequently overline(X_r)=(r! in K)^{-1}overline(x)^r and overline(Y_r)=(r! in K)^{-1}overline(y)^r, including r=0. Let W⊆N be a K-linear subspace invariant under overline(x),overline(y). Induction on r makes it invariant under their powers; subspace closure makes it invariant under scalar multiples and compositions of such maps. In particular it is invariant under
A_ij=d_K^{-1}(a_j in K)
       overline(X_{l-i}) overline(Y_l) overline(X_l) overline(Y_{l-j}).
This is exactly the earlier A_ij because the formula for Q_ij was an integral composition and B003 preserves it. No divided power with index greater than l is used. The generic statement B104 is precisely this invariance calculation from B004; the application here supplies its factorial identities via B102 and B003.

B105: the finite-dimensional matrix-unit argument.
For any field, any n>0, any n-dimensional space N and matrix units A_ij satisfying the relations just proved, let W be invariant under every A_ij. If W=0 there is nothing to show. Otherwise choose w∈W with w≠0. The identity w=Σ_i A_ii w implies that for some j, u=A_jj w≠0. For each i put z_i=A_ij w; it belongs to W. If Σ_i t_i z_i=0 is any K-linear relation, apply A_jk for an arbitrary k. The multiplication relation A_jk A_ij=δ_ki A_jj gives t_k u=0, and since u≠0 over a field, t_k=0. All coefficients vanish. Thus the n vectors z_i are linearly independent. B001, with dim_K N=n, implies that their span is N. Since each belongs to W, W=N. This proves B105.

Apply these results to the complete original target.
The preceding constructions used only the original arbitrary admissible M. B101 and B102 supplied the restricted integral maps, and its original basis supplied the integer basis required in B103. B103 gives nonzero N of dimension l+1 and the matrix-unit relations. For any K-linear subspace W_0⊆M⊗_Z K invariant under the original x,y,h, its image W=τ(W_0) is invariant under overline(x),overline(y), by the intertwining property. B104 then makes it invariant under all A_ij; B105 implies W=0 or W=N. The isomorphism τ returns W_0=0 or W_0=M⊗_Z K, and returns nonzero N to nonzero V(K). The supplied Lie-algebra construction, including characteristic 2, acts by these very induced lattice operators, so this proves exactly the required irreducibility as L(K)-module.

At l=0, 0!=1, P=X_0=Y_0=Id and there is one matrix unit; every calculation above still applies. At p=2 the possible l are 0 and 1 and all factorials that were inverted are still units. Nothing uses distinct h-eigenvalues in K; the h comparison occurred only over C. K was arbitrary throughout. There are no class-4 dependencies or additional source assumptions.

artifact.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
artifact.proof:
This proof retains exactly the original target and standing hypotheses. Fix any prime p, any field K of characteristic p, any integer λ with 0≤λ<p, the given complex irreducible highest-weight sl2-module V=V(λ) of dimension λ+1, its Chevalley operators x,y,h satisfying [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h, the given v≠0 with xv=0 and hv=λv, and ANY admissible lattice M of the problem. All divided powers X_r=x^r/r!, Y_r=y^r/r! for r≥0 preserve M by its U_Z-stability. Products of endomorphisms act rightmost first. Write l for the natural number equal to the nonnegative integer λ, and n=l+1. This is only a change of index domain, not a change of the parameter range. Integers in complex formulas are cast into C, and integers in reduced formulas are cast into K. The highest-weight module's irreducibility is retained as an original hypothesis; the calculation below needs only its stated dimension, commutators and highest-weight vector. No assumption of algebraic closure of K, and no restriction excluding p=2, is made.

The proof replaces the localization, fractional-ideal and localized-basis steps by integral multiples of matrix units followed directly by scalar extension. No new external theorem assumption is introduced. B001--B005 are the prepared native Mathlib facts. B101--B105 are internal lemmas proved here, not additional premises. Ordinary vector-space, tensor-product and finite-sum identities below are used with their defining algebraic properties; the registry is not a restriction on access to Mathlib.

B101: characteristic-zero string calculations and the divided-power basis.
For every i≥0, the commutator identities and induction give
h y^i v=(l-2i)y^i v,
x y^i v=i(l-i+1)y^{i-1}v for i≥1.
For completeness the h induction uses hy=yh-2y. For the x induction, x y^{i+1}v=(yx+h)y^i v, so the coefficient is i(l-i+1)+(l-2i)=(i+1)(l-i). The initial identities use xv=0 and hv=lv. These recurrences hold without assuming any termination of the y string.

For 0≤i≤l put e_i=(i!)^{-1}y^i v. Repeated use of the x recurrence gives
x^i y^i v=i! [l(l-1)...(l-i+1)] v.
The empty product for i=0 is one. Each factor in the nonempty descending product is a positive integer, hence nonzero in C, so e_i≠0 and x^i e_i=[l!/(l-i)!]v≠0. Also x^{i+1}e_i=0, since x^i e_i is a scalar multiple of v. To prove independence, suppose Σ_{i=0}^l c_i e_i=0 is a relation with a nonzero coefficient and choose its largest index m with c_m≠0. Applying x^m kills every term with index less than m; terms with index greater than m already have coefficient zero. It gives c_m [l!/(l-m)!]v=0, a contradiction. The family is therefore linearly independent, and B001 with dim_C V=n gives span equal to V; it is a basis.

Let u=y^{l+1}v. The same h recurrence gives hu=(-l-2)u. Expand u=Σ_i t_i e_i in the basis. Since he_i=(l-2i)e_i, comparison of coefficients gives 2(l+1-i)t_i=0 for every 0≤i≤l. This is a nonzero complex multiplier, so every t_i=0. Thus u=0, and all higher y powers of v vanish. The x recurrence and the definition of e_i now give
xe_0=0, xe_i=(l-i+1)e_{i-1} (1≤i≤l),
ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} (i<l), ye_l=0,
he_i=(l-2i)e_i.
Iterating the first and second formulas and dividing by r! in C yields
X_r e_i=choose(l-i+r,r)e_{i-r} if r≤i, and zero if r>i;
Y_r e_i=choose(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r≤l, and zero otherwise.
Indeed the first coefficient before division by r! is the product (l-i+1)...(l-i+r), and the second is (i+1)...(i+r); their factorial quotients are the displayed binomial coefficients. When the indices leave the string, a zero endpoint is encountered. This also proves the formulas for r=0, where both operators are the identity. This proves B101 from the elementary recurrences and B001.

B102: integral multiples of all matrix units.
Let E_ij be the complex-linear map taking e_j to e_i and all other e_k to zero, for 0≤i,j≤l. These are definitions relative to the basis just proved. Set
P=Y_l X_l, c_j=choose(l,j), a_j=j!(l-j)!, d=l!,
T_ij=X_{l-i} P Y_{l-j}, Q_ij=a_j T_ij.
All indices in these products are nonnegative and at most l. X_l kills e_k for k<l and sends e_l to e_0, and Y_l sends e_0 to e_l, so P=E_ll. Moreover X_{l-i} e_l=e_i. If k<j, Y_{l-j} e_k either lies strictly below e_l or is zero; if k>j, it is zero because the index is past l; on e_j it equals c_j e_l. Hence T_ij=c_j E_ij. The ordinary factorial identity
j!(l-j)! choose(l,j)=l!
for j≤l now gives the exact identity Q_ij=d E_ij in End_C(V).

Every factor X_r,Y_r preserves M, and a_j is an integer, so Q_ij restricts to a Z-linear endomorphism of M. On V the basis calculation gives E_ij E_kt=δ_jk E_it and Σ_i E_ii=Id. Thus, on M, the restricted operators satisfy
Q_ij Q_kt = d Q_it if j=k, and 0 if j≠k,
Σ_i Q_ii=d Id_M.
To justify restriction of identities, evaluate the equal complex maps on m∈M; the inclusion M⊆V is injective, so the values agree already in M. There is no division by d on M in this step. The same restriction argument gives r! X_r=x^r and r! Y_r=y^r on M for all natural r, directly from the definitions in C. Here x=X_1 and y=Y_1; h preserves M as well since h=xy-yx. These restrictions are the original lattice operators. This proves B102 using B101.

The given integer basis of M is also a complex basis of V. It therefore has exactly n elements: the finite-dimensional complex basis-cardinality theorem B005 gives this after indexing it by its finite cardinality. A basis of a finite-dimensional space is finite, so the indexing set can be replaced by Fin n. This is a reindexing of the given arbitrary lattice basis, not the choice of the minimal divided-power lattice. In particular M has a Z-basis indexed by Fin n.

B103: scalar extension, tensor-order compatibility, and normalized matrix units.
Use N=K⊗_Z M as the working representation of the original V(K)=M⊗_Z K. Here K is a Z-algebra through its integer map. The maps
τ:M⊗_Z K→K⊗_Z M, τ(m⊗c)=c⊗m,
σ:K⊗_Z M→M⊗_Z K, σ(c⊗m)=m⊗c
are defined by the balanced bilinear maps on pure tensors. For z∈Z, the balance check is c⊗(zm)=(zc)⊗m, and the reverse map has the same check. The K-action on the original tensor product is on its K factor. Both maps commute with that action, as may be checked on m⊗c and then finite sums. Their composites are the identity on pure tensors and hence on the whole tensor products. Thus τ is a K-linear isomorphism. For every integer endomorphism f of M it intertwines m⊗c↦f(m)⊗c with c⊗m↦c⊗f(m); again this is the same equality on each pure tensor. This establishes compatibility with the original action, rather than changing the reduction being studied.

By B002 an integer basis b_0,...,b_l of M gives the K-basis 1⊗b_0,...,1⊗b_l of N. By B005, dim_K N=n; this basis also makes N finite-dimensional. It is nonempty (n=l+1>0) and its vectors are nonzero, so N≠0.

Let F:End_Z(M)→End_K(N) be the Z-algebra homomorphism of B003 and put a bar over the scalar-extended lattice maps. B003 transports sums, compositions, powers, the identity and integer scalar multiples. B004, applied to r=l<p, says that d_K, the image of d=l! in K, is a unit and in particular nonzero. Define
A_ij=d_K^{-1} overline(Q_ij).
Transporting the integral identities of B102 gives
overline(Q_ij) overline(Q_kt)=δ_jk d_K overline(Q_it),
Σ_i overline(Q_ii)=d_K Id_N.
Scalar multiplication commutes with K-linear endomorphisms, so multiplication by d_K^{-2} in the first equality and d_K^{-1} in the second yields
A_ij A_kt=δ_jk A_it,  Σ_i A_ii=Id_N.
This proves B103 with B002--B005 and the integral identities as its stated premises; its proof applies to any integral module and operators satisfying those premises.

B104: invariance under the original generators implies invariance under these matrix units.
For every 0≤r≤l<p, B004 gives r! nonzero in K. Applying B003 to the restricted factorial identities of B102 gives
(r! in K) overline(X_r)=overline(x)^r,
(r! in K) overline(Y_r)=overline(y)^r.
Consequently overline(X_r)=(r! in K)^{-1}overline(x)^r and overline(Y_r)=(r! in K)^{-1}overline(y)^r, including r=0. Let W⊆N be a K-linear subspace invariant under overline(x),overline(y). Induction on r makes it invariant under their powers; subspace closure makes it invariant under scalar multiples and compositions of such maps. In particular it is invariant under
A_ij=d_K^{-1}(a_j in K)
       overline(X_{l-i}) overline(Y_l) overline(X_l) overline(Y_{l-j}).
This is exactly the earlier A_ij because the formula for Q_ij was an integral composition and B003 preserves it. No divided power with index greater than l is used. The generic statement B104 is precisely this invariance calculation from B004; the application here supplies its factorial identities via B102 and B003.

B105: the finite-dimensional matrix-unit argument.
For any field, any n>0, any n-dimensional space N and matrix units A_ij satisfying the relations just proved, let W be invariant under every A_ij. If W=0 there is nothing to show. Otherwise choose w∈W with w≠0. The identity w=Σ_i A_ii w implies that for some j, u=A_jj w≠0. For each i put z_i=A_ij w; it belongs to W. If Σ_i t_i z_i=0 is any K-linear relation, apply A_jk for an arbitrary k. The multiplication relation A_jk A_ij=δ_ki A_jj gives t_k u=0, and since u≠0 over a field, t_k=0. All coefficients vanish. Thus the n vectors z_i are linearly independent. B001, with dim_K N=n, implies that their span is N. Since each belongs to W, W=N. This proves B105.

Apply these results to the complete original target.
The preceding constructions used only the original arbitrary admissible M. B101 and B102 supplied the restricted integral maps, and its original basis supplied the integer basis required in B103. B103 gives nonzero N of dimension l+1 and the matrix-unit relations. For any K-linear subspace W_0⊆M⊗_Z K invariant under the original x,y,h, its image W=τ(W_0) is invariant under overline(x),overline(y), by the intertwining property. B104 then makes it invariant under all A_ij; B105 implies W=0 or W=N. The isomorphism τ returns W_0=0 or W_0=M⊗_Z K, and returns nonzero N to nonzero V(K). The supplied Lie-algebra construction, including characteristic 2, acts by these very induced lattice operators, so this proves exactly the required irreducibility as L(K)-module.

At l=0, 0!=1, P=X_0=Y_0=Id and there is one matrix unit; every calculation above still applies. At p=2 the possible l are 0 and 1 and all factorials that were inverted are still units. Nothing uses distinct h-eigenvalues in K; the h comparison occurred only over C. K was arbitrary throughout. There are no class-4 dependencies or additional source assumptions.

artifact.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

x y^i v=i(l-i+1)y^{i-1}v for i≥1.

For 0≤i≤l put e_i=(i!)^{-1}y^i v. Repeated use of the x recurrence gives
x^i y^i v=i! [l(l-1)...(l-i+1)] v.

The family is therefore linearly independent, and B001 with dim_C V=n gives span equal to V; it is a basis.

ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} (i<l), ye_l=0,
he_i=(l-2i)e_i.

X_r e_i=choose(l-i+r,r)e_{i-r} if r≤i, and zero if r>i;
Y_r e_i=choose(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r≤l, and zero otherwise.
Indeed the first coefficient before division by r! is the product (l-i+1)...(l-i+r), and the second is (i+1)...(i+r); their factorial quotients are the displayed binomial coefficients. When the indices leave the string, a zero endpoint is encountered. This also proves the formulas for r=0, where both operators are the identity. The given integer basis of M is also a complex basis of V. It therefore has exactly n elements: the finite-dimensional complex basis-cardinality theorem B005 gives this after indexing it by its finite cardinality. A basis of a finite-dimensional space is finite, so the indexing set can be replaced by Fin n. This is a reindexing of the given arbitrary lattice basis, not the choice of the minimal divided-power lattice. In particular M has a Z-basis indexed by Fin n.

τ:M⊗_Z K→K⊗_Z M, τ(m⊗c)=c⊗m,
σ:K⊗_Z M→M⊗_Z K, σ(c⊗m)=m⊗c

Their composites are the identity on pure tensors and hence on the whole tensor products. Thus τ is a K-linear isomorphism. For any field, any n>0, any n-dimensional space N and matrix units A_ij satisfying the relations just proved, let W be invariant under every A_ij. If W=0 there is nothing to show. Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

All divided powers X_r=x^r/r!, Y_r=y^r/r! for r≥0 preserve M by its U_Z-stability. Products of endomorphisms act rightmost first. Write l for the natural number equal to the nonnegative integer λ, and n=l+1. This is only a change of index domain, not a change of the parameter range. Integers in complex formulas are cast into C, and integers in reduced formulas are cast into K. The highest-weight module's irreducibility is retained as an original hypothesis; the calculation below needs only its stated dimension, commutators and highest-weight vector. No assumption of algebraic closure of K, and no restriction excluding p=2, is made.

The proof replaces the localization, fractional-ideal and localized-basis steps by integral multiples of matrix units followed directly by scalar extension. No new external theorem assumption is introduced. B001--B005 are the prepared native Mathlib facts. B101--B105 are internal lemmas proved here, not additional premises. Ordinary vector-space, tensor-product and finite-sum identities below are used with their defining algebraic properties; the registry is not a restriction on access to Mathlib.

B101: characteristic-zero string calculations and the divided-power basis.
For every i≥0, the commutator identities and induction give

x y^i v=i(l-i+1)y^{i-1}v for i≥1.
For completeness the h induction uses hy=yh-2y. For the x induction, x y^{i+1}v=(yx+h)y^i v, so the coefficient is i(l-i+1)+(l-2i)=(i+1)(l-i). The initial identities use xv=0 and hv=lv. These recurrences hold without assuming any termination of the y string.

For 0≤i≤l put e_i=(i!)^{-1}y^i v. Repeated use of the x recurrence gives
x^i y^i v=i! [l(l-1)...(l-i+1)] v.
The empty product for i=0 is one. Each factor in the nonempty descending product is a positive integer, hence nonzero in C, so e_i≠0 and x^i e_i=[l!/(l-i)!]v≠0.
